newsitem.title: USA: US rail freight traffic up sharply from year ago.
newsitem.headline: US rail freight traffic up sharply from year ago.

text.p: U.S. rail freight traffic -- measured in carloads and ton-miles -- rose sharply in the week ended January 11 from the same week a year ago, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.

AAR said carloads in the week totaled 324,476, up 8.7 percent from 298,450 in the year-ago week. Ton-miles stood at 25.6 billion, up 10.8 percent from 23.1 billion a year ago. A ton-mile is one ton of freight hauled one mile.
Intermodal volume, which does not include carloads, climbed 7.9 percent to 152,051 trailers and containers from 140,889 in the year-ago week.

"Traffic a year ago was severely affected by the 'Blizzard of '96' which sharply curtailed rail operations in much of the eastern United States," AAR senior assistant vice president Craig Rockey said.
AAR said the biggest carload gains from the year-ago week were in coal, up 21.5 percent to 130,497 carloads from 107,447, and in chemicals, up 14.1 percent to 31,175 carloads from 27,317 a year ago.

Carloads of metals and related products also rose 12 percent to 11,520 in the January 11 week from 10,284 in the year-ago week, while carloads of motor vehicles and equipment increased 11.3 percent to 18,482 from 16,609. Petroleum products rose 10.3 percent to 5,644 carloads from 5,118 last year.

AAR said the biggest carload declines from a year ago were of grain, down 14.2 percent to 23,621 carloads in the week from 27,516 last year, and metallic ores, which declined 14.1 percent to 13,152 carloads from 15,319.
In the first two weeks of 1997, AAR said that ton-miles rose eight percent from the same period in 1996. Carloads were up 5.9 percent while intermodal freight rose 3.8 percent, it said.

In a separate account, AAR said U.S. intermodal traffic to Canada in the January 11 week totaled 22,732 trailers and containers, up 10.6 percent from the year-ago week. But it said U.S. carloads to Canada were 46,644, down 9.5 percent from a year ago.
